The ESPN mobile app is also picking up an AI search feature, giving users instant access to sports data, news, stats, and other historical information. articles.excerpt: Your stand-up routine lasts 45 minutes. No one in that room thinks it's a stand-up routine. You're basically giving a status update with unnecessary details. Also, the individual inquiring about what…
articles.body: Your stand-up routine lasts 45 minutes. No one in that room thinks it's a stand-up routine. You're basically giving a status update with unnecessary details. Also, the individual inquiring about what is blocking you is not actually helping to resolve the issue. The framework isn't the problem People enjoy criticizing Agile methods, such as the lengthy 45-minute daily stand-up meetings. The 45-minute standups, the story points that somehow became a performance review, the sprint that never ends. However, blaming Agile would be similar to blaming the hammer for the hole in your wall. Despite everything, statistics show that people are still using it. Digital.ai's 17th Annual State of Agile Report from January 2024 surveyed 788 software pros and found 71% of organizations use Agile.

articles.title: Cómo solucionar el error \"Text content does not match server-rendered HTML\" en Next.js App Router
articles.excerpt: Cómo solucionar el error "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" en Next.js App Router Este error ocurre cuando el HTML generado en el servidor (SSR/SSG) no coincide con el árbol de React g…
articles.body: Cómo solucionar el error "Text content does not match server-rendered HTML" en Next.js App Router Este error ocurre cuando el HTML generado en el servidor (SSR/SSG) no coincide con el árbol de React generado durante la primera renderización en el cliente. React detecta la inconsistencia durante el proceso de hydration y lanza una advertencia crítica que puede romper la funcionalidad de tu app. Causa raíz La mayoría de los casos provienen de código no idempotente entre SSR y CSR , es decir, código que produce resultados diferentes dependiendo de si se ejecuta en el servidor o en el navegador. Las causas más frecuentes: Uso de Date.now() , new Date() , Math.random() o APIs dependientes del tiempo en el renderizado. Acceso directo a window , localStorage , navigator , etc. sin protección.
articles.author: Erick Eduardo Ramos

articles.body: TL;DR Aptoide Games is coming to Google Play in the US, letting Android users install a competing app store without sideloading an APK. The move follows years of legal pressure from Epic Games and Google’s recent changes allowing qualifying third-party app stores onto the US Play Store. This could make alternative Android app stores more accessible, giving users new ways to discover apps and developers more options for distributing them. Google Play is about to do something that would have sounded pretty strange not too long ago: let you download another app store from inside Google’s own app store. Aptoide has announced that Aptoide Games, its gaming-focused Android marketplace, is coming to Google Play in the US.

articles.title: Why I Don't Put Tenant-Specific Validation in My FastAPI Endpoints
articles.excerpt: Multi-tenant applications have a way of turning simple endpoints into surprisingly complicated pieces of code. At first, tenant-specific validation seems harmless. You have two tenants with different…
articles.body: Multi-tenant applications have a way of turning simple endpoints into surprisingly complicated pieces of code. At first, tenant-specific validation seems harmless. You have two tenants with different limits, so you write something like: if tenant == " acme " : max_quantity = 100 elif tenant == " globex " : max_quantity = 10 It works. The problem isn't the first if . The problem is what happens after there are ten more rules. When the endpoint starts knowing too much I prefer an endpoint to answer one main question: What should the application do with this request?

articles.title: How SSL Certificates Work: Chains of Trust and Why Yours Expired
articles.excerpt: Your site was fine yesterday. This morning every browser is throwing a full-page security warning, monitoring is screaming, and nobody deployed anything. A certificate expired. That's it. One of the m…
articles.body: Your site was fine yesterday. This morning every browser is throwing a full-page security warning, monitoring is screaming, and nobody deployed anything. A certificate expired. That's it. One of the most common self-inflicted outages in software, and it happens to companies with entire infrastructure teams who should know better. You depend on certificates whether or not you understand them. And when they break, they break loudly and totally. There's no graceful degradation. Every visitor sees a scary red page. Quick naming note: everyone says "SSL certificate" but SSL is the retired protocol. The artifact is actually an X.509 certificate and the protocol is TLS. The name stuck out of habit.

articles.title: What Happens During a TLS Handshake?
articles.excerpt: Two machines that have never spoken before need to agree on a secret. They're communicating over a network where anyone can read every packet. And they need to pull this off in a few milliseconds, bef…
articles.body: Two machines that have never spoken before need to agree on a secret. They're communicating over a network where anyone can read every packet. And they need to pull this off in a few milliseconds, before you notice the page loading slowly. That's the TLS handshake. Every HTTPS connection starts with one. It's the reason your connections have a latency floor, and it's where most TLS misconfigurations live. I covered what HTTPS actually protects in a previous post . This one is the handshake itself, the message flow I promised would get its own post. 🧠 Three jobs before any data flows Before a single byte of application data moves, the handshake needs to accomplish three things: Agree on a shared symmetric key .

articles.title: When Crypto Price Charts Learned to Sing: Building Real-Time Sonification for 1400+ Trading Pairs
articles.excerpt: I never intended to create an audio trading app. It happened by accident during a particularly frustrating week where my eyes couldn't keep up with fourteen monitor windows simultaneously. I was watch…
articles.body: I never intended to create an audio trading app. It happened by accident during a particularly frustrating week where my eyes couldn't keep up with fourteen monitor windows simultaneously. I was watching BTC oscillate around $62k while SOL dropped another 0.92%, and my brain just... seized. Too many numbers. Too much noise. What if instead of looking, I listened ? That question led me down a rabbit hole called sonification—the practice of converting data into sound. Today, August 2026, I'm running Confrontational Meditation®, and we're sonifying real-time price movements across 1400+ cryptocurrency pairs. It's unconventional. It's chaotic. It's also the clearest way I've ever understood market movement. The Problem With Eyes Traditional charting is exhausting.

Android phone backups are bigger, WhatsApp chats count against your limit, and between 4K video backups and high-resolution photography, it’s easy to fill up that free storage in months if not weeks. articles.title: Could the northern lights be visible during the total solar eclipse on Aug.12? Maybe.
articles.excerpt: A total solar eclipse and the northern lights at the same time? Experts explain why it's possible, but the odds are stacked against it.
articles.body: On Aug. 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse will sweep across Earth, giving skywatchers across Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain an incredible view of totality. As the moon completely covers the sun, day will briefly turn to twilight, revealing the sun's faint outer atmosphere, the corona. But could totality reveal something else too? Although totality never produces true nighttime darkness, it does briefly dim the sky to roughly the brightness of twilight. Since eclipse chasers in Greenland and Iceland will be in the auroral zone — the geographic zone around Earth's magnetic pole where auroras are most frequently seen — it's natural to wonder whether the two phenomena could appear together. The answer is yes — but only if everything falls perfectly into place.

articles.excerpt: Director Will Gluck revealed that he “cut out so much” nudity from One Night Only because he believes modern movie audiences are now too uncomfortable seeing it on screen.
articles.body: Director Will Gluck (Easy A, Anyone But You) has revealed that he “cut out so much” nudity from his new romantic comedy One Night Only because he believes modern movie audiences are now too uncomfortable seeing it on screen. Speaking with Variety , Gluck admitted research that has found Gen Z and Gen Alpha want to see less sex on screen was very much a concern while making One Night Only. “The answer is 100% yes,” said Gluck. “I went through this on two movies. I have long pages of empirical data about it. The only thing is I don’t think it’s just Gen Z and Gen Alpha. I believe it’s been a societal shift from taking nudity in adult situations and putting them on your phones at home for everybody.
articles.author: Luke Reilly

articles.excerpt: House of the Dragon's season 3 finale finally reveals when The Prince That Was Promised goes from Targaryen family secret to Westeros legend.
articles.body: Rhaenyra Targaryen is just about fed up. The castle she finally conquered at the start of House of the Dragon season 3 has become more like a prison where she's forced to babysit her political rivals, hide from her enemies, and field complaints from the local commonfolk while they insult her behind her back. But Rhaenyra (Emma D’Arcy) knows she was born for more than this. She was meant for greatness — a belief that was passed down by her father and then reinforced by a witchy prophecy seen by her husband/uncle Daemon (Matt Smith).
articles.author: Jake Kleinman

articles.title: House of the Dragon Season 3 Ending Explained and Book Differences
articles.excerpt: Unpack the House of the Dragon Season 3 finale ending, including key betrayals, deaths, dragon devastation, and the biggest book-to-show changes from Fire & Blood.
articles.body: Spoilers follow for both House of the Dragon and the book Fire & Blood . Season 3 of House of the Dragon has come to an end, and with it so too has any chance of Rhaenyra Targaryen (Emma D’Arcy) being the hero of this show. While her heel turn wasn’t as abrupt as and was far better developed than how Game of Thrones handled Daenerys’ descent into villainy , it seems the Iron Throne truly does corrupt, physically or morally, every Targaryen who occupies it. By the final moments of this episode, Rhaenyra has fully gone over to the Dark Side. She ultimately chooses to sacrifice her humanity in pursuit of power and to win the war against the Greens.

articles.title: House of the Dragon Season 3 Finale Recap and Review
articles.excerpt: House of the Dragon Season 3 Finale Recap and Review: There’s little sense of an ending here, but this spectacular battle left everything to play for in the final season.
articles.body: Full spoilers follow for House of the Dragon Season 3, Episode 8, “The Traitors of Tumbleton.” Back in the day, Game of Thrones typically delivered its big action beats in a season’s penultimate episode and spent the finale wrapping up loose ends and setting the stakes for the following year . House of the Dragon is a different beast: this season began and ended with all-out war, and if anything, this finale leaves too many loose ends dangling. If it’s less punch-the-air satisfying than the season opener, it may have more consequential revelations for what’s to come. articles.title: Exploring 'very low Earth orbit': The world's 1st air-breathing satellite thruster could soon get a test run
articles.excerpt: Air-breathing electric propulsion could help satellites explore a new frontier, one that lies quite close to our planet.
articles.body: A new way to move around Earth's outer atmosphere could soon get a field test. The Spanish company Kreios Space plans to launch into orbit the world's first satellite that uses scooped-up air to push it forward, the company announced on Tuesday (Aug. 4). The technology Kreios Space has been developing is called air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP). It relies on air sourced from Earth's atmosphere, which is then heated up, ionized and expelled to generate thrust. Diagram showing the different types of orbit around Earth. (Image credit: ESA) This method will allow satellites in very low Earth orbit (VLEO) — the region from roughly 60 miles to 250 miles (100 to 400 kilometers) above our planet — to counteract atmospheric drag without the aid of liquid fuel.
